blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A global sanctions programme is never truly complete. Even if every current list were screened correctly, new names appear every week, secondary sanctions reach across borders, and different jurisdictions impose contradictory rules. The task of a compliance programme is not to promise no mistakes, but to demonstrate that the organisation takes the problem as seriously as the regulators expect — and that, when an issue surfaces, it is caught early, escalated properly, and learned from openly inside the company.

The three pillars are coverage, escalation and culture. Coverage means automated screening at every relevant moment: counterparty onboarding, contract signing, payment execution, shipment dispatch. Escalation means a clear path for borderline cases to reach a specialist within hours, not weeks. Culture means that frontline teams feel safer raising a concern than quietly ignoring it, and that compliance officers are treated as strategic partners, not annoying gatekeepers.

Even though most sanctions incidents are caught by the coverage layer, it is the culture layer that prevents the worst outcomes. A company that pretends to be clean is one that will eventually be publicly embarrassed. A company that treats compliance as a genuine discipline rarely ends up on the front page.

items.q: According to the text, what is the task of a compliance programme?
options: To demonstrate that the organisation takes the problem as seriously as regulators expect
To keep every incident confidential inside the company
To screen only at the moment of payment execution
To guarantee that no mistakes will ever occur
items.why: "not to promise no mistakes, but to demonstrate that the organisation takes the problem as seriously as the regulators expect".

items.q: What are the three pillars named in the text?
options: Coverage, escalation and culture
Onboarding, contracting and shipping
Regulation, jurisdiction and enforcement
Screening, reporting and auditing
items.why: "The three pillars are coverage, escalation and culture."

items.q: What does escalation mean, according to the text?
options: Automated screening at every relevant moment
A gradual increase in the number of names screened
A clear path for borderline cases to reach a specialist within hours
The public disclosure of every compliance breach
items.why: "Escalation means a clear path for borderline cases to reach a specialist within hours, not weeks."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A strong screening system alone is enough to prevent the worst outcomes.
Compliance officers should be treated as strategic partners.
New sanctioned names appear continuously, so screening is never finished.
Coverage catches most sanctions incidents.
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma que é a camada de cultura, não a de cobertura, que evita os piores desfechos.

items.q: What does the contrast between a company that "pretends to be clean" and one that "treats compliance as a genuine discipline" suggest?
options: Screening technology matters more than internal honesty
Compliance is mostly a matter of good public relations
Only large companies are ever publicly embarrassed
Honesty about risk is safer than a flawless public image
items.why: Inferência: o autor valoriza a disciplina real e o reconhecimento do problema acima da aparência de perfeição.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte apresentando o redesenho do programa de sanções após um quase-incidente. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for making the time. I want to walk you through what the near-miss in the new subsidiary actually taught us, because it wasn't a technology failure — the screening tool flagged the counterparty correctly.

What went wrong was the second step. The alert sat in a shared inbox for eleven days before anyone looked at it. By the time it reached a specialist, the payment had almost gone out. So although our coverage held, our escalation didn't. That gap is exactly what I'm proposing to close.

Here is what I'm asking for. First, borderline cases route straight to a named specialist within hours — no shared inboxes, no waiting on someone's leave calendar. Second, and this is the harder part, we change how the frontline feels. Right now a junior analyst who raises a concern worries about slowing down a deal. That has to flip. I'd rather field a hundred false alarms than have one person stay quiet.

Even though the numbers say coverage catches most things, it's the culture that keeps us off the front page. A team that trusts compliance will tell us early. A team that fears it will hope the problem quietly disappears — and it never does.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Charlotte, what did the near-miss actually reveal?
options: The coverage held, but the escalation broke down
The subsidiary had no compliance programme at all
The screening tool failed to flag the counterparty
The regulators had changed the rules overnight
items.why: "although our coverage held, our escalation didn't" — a ferramenta sinalizou; o alerta ficou parado.

items.q: Why did the alert become dangerous?
options: It was deleted by mistake
It sat in a shared inbox for eleven days before anyone looked at it
The payment had already been sent weeks earlier
The specialist rejected it incorrectly
items.why: "The alert sat in a shared inbox for eleven days before anyone looked at it."

items.q: What is Charlotte's first proposed change?
options: Route borderline cases straight to a named specialist within hours
Reduce the number of alerts the system generates
Move all compliance work to the subsidiary
Replace the screening software entirely
items.why: "borderline cases route straight to a named specialist within hours — no shared inboxes".

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by "I'd rather field a hundred false alarms than have one person stay quiet"?
options: False alarms are cheaper than real incidents
The team should stop raising concerns unless they are certain
She prefers over-reporting to silence, even if most concerns turn out to be nothing
She wants to reduce the total number of alerts
items.why: Inferência: ela aceita muitos alarmes falsos como preço para que ninguém deixe de falar.

items.q: What does Charlotte imply about a team that fears compliance?
options: It performs better under pressure
It will hope the problem disappears on its own, which it never does
It will report problems faster to avoid blame
It will always escalate borderline cases correctly
items.why: Inferência: "A team that fears it will hope the problem quietly disappears — and it never does."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Secondary sanctions can punish a firm that never touched the sanctioning country's market." Secondary sanctions are…
options: penalties aimed at third parties who deal with a sanctioned entity
a milder, optional set of rules for small firms
restrictions limited to a single jurisdiction
sanctions that apply only after a first warning
items.why: Sanções secundárias atingem terceiros que negociam com a parte sancionada — alcançam além das fronteiras.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Compliance rests on three ___: coverage, escalation and culture."
options: gatekeepers
inboxes
shipments
pillars
items.why: Pillar = pilar, cada um dos sustentáculos do programa.

items.q: "Screening at onboarding stops the riskiest counterparties before any money moves." Onboarding here means…
options: the dispatch of a shipment
the final payment of a contract
an internal staff training session
the process of taking on a new counterparty or client
items.why: Onboarding = integração/entrada de uma nova contraparte ao sistema.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The case was ___ — not clearly permitted, not clearly forbidden — so it needed a specialist's judgement."
options: secondary
borderline
automated
frontline
items.why: Borderline = limítrofe, um caso na zona cinzenta que exige escalonamento.

items.q: "Treating officers as gatekeepers makes teams route around them." A gatekeeper is…
options: a shared inbox for alerts
someone who controls access or approval to something
an external regulator
a junior analyst on the frontline
items.why: Gatekeeper = guardião que controla passagem/aprovação; a lição defende vê-los como parceiros, não obstáculos.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre compliance e sanções. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Legal still has to sign off on the new escalation policy." To sign off on means to…
options: quietly ignore
postpone indefinitely
leak to the press
formally approve
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new screening rules subsidiary by subsidiary." To roll out means to…
options: outsource entirely
cancel in secret
implement in stages
audit retroactively
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, unidade a unidade.

items.q: "Two country heads pushed back on the tighter payment controls." They…
options: rewrote them overnight
resisted or objected to them
approved them without comment
forgot to read them
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed to escalate borderline cases but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it out to completion
escalated everything at once
documented it too thoroughly
delegated it to the regulator
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A named owner and a two-hour SLA will actually move the needle on escalation speed." This means it will…
options: make a noticeable difference
confuse the frontline
take years to measure
raise legal costs
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível.
